description: A guide to the best hill stations for summer in India, from April to June: the Himalayan towns of Himachal and Uttarakhand, Kashmir's meadows, Darjeeling, Sikkim and Shillong in the east, the Nilgiris, Kodaikanal and Munnar in the south, and high valleys that open in June, with how to avoid the crowds.

intro: Summer, from April to June, is the classic hill-station season in India: school holidays, hot plains and pleasant mountain days. It is also when the famous towns are busiest, so choosing well matters as much as where you go.
Himalayan hill stations are coolest; the southern hills are pleasant but milder; and some high valleys, such as Spiti and Ladakh, only open fully in June.
quickAnswer: The best hill stations for summer in India are Shimla, Manali, Dharamshala and Dalhousie in Himachal Pradesh; Mussoorie, Nainital, Kausani and Munsiyari in Uttarakhand; Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg in Kashmir; Darjeeling, Gangtok and Shillong in the east; and Ooty, Kodaikanal and Munnar in the south. Book early for May and June, travel midweek, and consider quieter towns nearby.
takeaways: April to June is peak season; the famous towns are crowded, especially in late May and June.
Kashmir's meadows and Sikkim's valleys are at their greenest in May and June.
Ladakh, Spiti and Lahaul open fully from around June, when the passes clear.
The southern hills are pleasant in April and May, but busy; Ooty and Kodaikanal need an e-pass for most outside vehicles.
Pre-monsoon storms can arrive in June in the east and south.

sections.heading: High valleys that open in summer
paras: From around June, when snow is cleared from the passes, the high valleys of Lahaul, Spiti and Ladakh open for road trips. They are cool, dry and outside the monsoon's reach, but high enough to need acclimatisation. Rohtang Pass opens in summer with an online permit, while the Atal Tunnel gives year-round access to Lahaul.

sections.heading: Beating the crowds
list: Travel midweek and avoid long weekends.
Stay a little outside the main town: Landour instead of Mussoorie's Mall, Bhimtal instead of Nainital, Coonoor instead of Ooty.
Choose quieter hills: Kausani, Lansdowne, Chail, Kalimpong, Yercaud, Sakleshpur.
Start sightseeing early, before day-trippers arrive.
Book stays and transport weeks ahead for late May and June.

sections.heading: How cool is cool?
paras: Hill stations are much cooler than the plains, but they are not cold in summer. Mid-altitude Himalayan towns such as Shimla, Mussoorie and Darjeeling usually have mild days and cool evenings; the southern hills are pleasant rather than cold; and lower hill towns such as Mount Abu, Lonavala or Pachmarhi can still be warm by day. Pack a light jacket for evenings everywhere.

sections.heading: Summer with children
paras: Summer holidays mean most families travel in May and June. Choose towns with easy walks, lakes and short drives, such as Nainital, Mussoorie, Shimla, Ooty or Kodaikanal, and plan no more than one long drive every few days. Toy trains, boating, pony rides and gardens keep younger children busy, while older children often enjoy Manali's adventure activities or Darjeeling's zoo and mountaineering institute.

sections.heading: Summer combinations
list: Shimla and Manali with a night in Kasol or Jibhi.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates, and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
Summer storms can bring hail and sudden cold; carry a waterproof layer.
Stay hydrated and use sunscreen; the sun is strong at altitude.

faqs.q: Which hill station is best in summer?
faqs.a: Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie, Nainital, Gulmarg, Darjeeling, Gangtok and Ooty are popular; Kausani, Kalimpong and Coonoor are quieter.

faqs.q: Which is the coolest place in India in summer?
faqs.a: High places such as Ladakh, Spiti, Sonamarg and Lachung stay coldest; among hill towns, Gulmarg and Munsiyari are among the coolest.

faqs.q: Where can I go in June?
faqs.a: Kashmir, Lahaul, Spiti, Ladakh, Munsiyari and Tawang are good in June; the south and east start getting monsoon rain.

faqs.q: Which hill stations are less crowded in summer?
faqs.a: Kausani, Lansdowne, Chail, Kalimpong, Coonoor, Yercaud and Sakleshpur.

faqs.q: Do I need to book ahead in summer?
faqs.a: Yes, especially for late May and June and long weekends.

faqs.q: Is Mount Abu good in summer?
faqs.a: It is cooler than the Rajasthan plains, but days can still be warm; mornings and evenings are pleasant.
